latin.220:
§. V.
Postremum Seculi ejusdem Reformationis primi molimen Concordiae Protestanticae, non in Germania quidem, sed in Polonia An. 1570. susceptum omnium perfectissimum SENDOMIRIENSE est, Consensus Sendomiriensis cognomine celebratum.
latin.221: Hujus verò, cùm non tantùm editionem novam Latino-Germanicam nunc paraverimus, sed & Perfectionem ejus, quâ Consensus Protestanticos ad unum omnes, multis post se parasangis relinquit, in peculiari praemissa Prefatione, novem evidentissimis argumentis adstruxerimus, solutis etiam, quae hic opponi vulgò solent, exceptionibus cunctis, non est, cur vel causae ejus dicendae, vel excellentiae commendandae immoremur amplius.
latin.222: imitationem potiùs tàm salutaris, cordati ac Christiani prorsus facti atque exempli, Protestantibus in Germania nostra, aliisque vicinis regnis septentrionalibus, quin in orbe Europaeo integro, ubicunque tandem Protestantes utriusque partis inveniuntur, totô pectore apprecati,
latin.223: acquiesuri de cetero in Judicio B. Hornbeckii de hoc Consensu, quod semper & nostrum faciemus, quando: Nulla, inquit, hâc melior vel augustior & perfectior Confessio facta unquam fuit, quae Politice & Ecclesiasticè approbata, & quam jucundâ & illustri admodum Sacrorum Communione invicem confirmarunt.
latin.224: Ab utraque parte haud semel Confessiones & Ecclesias mutuo agnoscunt pro veris: Convenimus, ut quemadmodum illi (August. Conf. Socii) nos, nostrasque Ecclesias & Confessionem nostram in hac Synodo publicatam & Fratrum, Orthodoxas testantur [ita Bohemicae Confessionis Socii de se & Helveticae Confessionis sociis loquuntur] sic etiam nos illorum Ecclesias [puta Augustanae Confessionis Sociorum] eodem Christiano amore prosequamur & Orthodoxas fateamur, Miscel. Sacr. Part. 1. p. 703.

pass_a.220: §. V. The last Consociation attempt of Protestant Concord of the first Reformation century, not indeed in Germany, but undertaken in Poland in the year 1570, is the most perfect of all, the SENDOMIR one, celebrated under the surname of the Sendomir Consensus.
pass_a.221: But of this, since we have not only now prepared a new Latino-German edition, but have also established its Perfection — by which it leaves all Protestant Consensuses to a one many parasangs behind itself — in a peculiar Prefatio prefixed, by nine most evident arguments, having also solved all the exceptions that are commonly wont to be opposed here, there is no reason why we should linger further either on stating its cause or on recommending its excellence.
pass_a.222: rather having prayed with the whole breast for the imitation of so salutary, wise, and altogether Christian a deed and example, to the Protestants in our Germany, and to other neighboring northern kingdoms, nay in the whole European world, wherever at length Protestants of either party are found,
pass_a.223: being about to rest thereafter in the Judgment of blessed Hornbeck concerning this Consensus, which we will always also make our own, when he says: No better or more august and more perfect Confession than this was ever made, which was approved Politically and Ecclesiastically, and which they confirmed mutually by a most joyful and illustrious Communion of sacred things.
pass_a.224: From either side they not once only mutually acknowledge Confessions and Churches as true: We have agreed, that just as those (Associates of the Augsburg Confession) testify that we, and our Churches and our Confession published in this Synod and of the Brethren, are Orthodox [so speak the Associates of the Bohemian Confession of themselves and of the associates of the Helvetic Confession], so also we may pursue their Churches [namely of the Associates of the Augsburg Confession] with the same Christian love and confess them Orthodox — Miscellaneous Sacred Things, Part 1, p. 703.

220: §. V. The last Consociation attempt at Protestant Concord in that first Reformation century was not in Germany but in Poland in 1570.
It is the most perfect of all — the Sendomir attempt, celebrated under the name Consensus Sendomiriensis.
221: Of this Consensus we have not only prepared a new Latino-German edition, but in a special Prefatio set out nine clearest arguments for the perfection by which it leaves every other Protestant consensus many parasangs behind — and we have answered all the usual objections.
So there is no need to linger further either stating its cause or praising its excellence.
222: Better to pray with whole heart that Protestants in our Germany, in the neighboring northern kingdoms, and throughout Europe — wherever either party’s Protestants are found — imitate so wholesome, clear-headed, and thoroughly Christian a deed and example.
223: For the rest we rest in blessed Hornbeck’s judgment on this Consensus — and we will always make it ours — when he says: no better, more august, or more perfect Confession than this was ever made.
It was approved politically and ecclesiastically, and they confirmed it mutually by a most joyful and illustrious communion of the sacraments.
224: From both sides they more than once acknowledge each other’s Confessions and churches as true.

We have agreed: just as the Augsburg Confession’s associates testify that we, our churches, and our Confession published in this synod of the Brethren are Orthodox — so the Bohemian Confession’s associates speak of themselves and of the Helvetic Confession’s associates — so also we will pursue their churches (the Augsburg associates’) with the same Christian love and confess them Orthodox (Hornbeck, Miscel. Sacr. Part 1, p. 703).
